name: ACT / ALOHA
summary: ALOHA is an open-source low-cost bimanual puppeteering setup; ACT is the policy trained on it. ACT predicts a chunk of about 100 future actions at once with a transformer CVAE, shortening the effective horizon and suppressing compounding error, while temporal ensembling across overlapping chunks smooths execution. Together they learn tasks like inserting a battery or opening a translucent condiment cup from roughly 50 demos at 80-90% success.
innovation: Action chunking: predict k steps at once to cut the compounding-error horizon by a factor of k.
Temporal ensembling of overlapping chunks for smooth, jitter-free real-time execution.
Open, affordable bimanual hardware that democratized dexterous data collection.
matters: Action chunking is now near-universal: pi-0, OpenVLA-OFT, GR00T and Diffusion Policy all use it.
ALOHA hardware and its clones became the standard bimanual research platform.
limits: Pure imitation from a fixed setup, with no language generalization and limited robustness to scene change.
lineage: Transformer sequence prediction applied to action chunks, on purpose-built cheap bimanual hardware.
